ing: pierced with a fork, or zest of 2 limes
st: Season the chicken with salt and half of the baharat. Heat the ghee in a wide heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Set it aside.
In the same pot, cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom and remaining baharat and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Return the chicken to the pot. Add the dried limes and [[2 cups]] hot water, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift the chicken out. Measure the liquid in the pot and add water to make [[3.5 cups]]. Bring to a boil and season with salt.
Drain the soaked rice and stir it into the pot. Boil for 3 minutes, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes.
Nestle the chicken on top of the rice, cover again, and steam off the heat for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice, scatter the cilantro, and serve with the chicken on top.
Melt the ghee in a pot over medium heat. Add the rinsed rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Add [[3.5 cups]] water, the salt and half of the cardamom. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile, put the sugar and [[0.5 cup]] water in a small saucepan and heat until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the saffron and simmer for 5 minutes until lightly syrupy. Add the dates and remaining cardamom.
Add the rose water and remove the syrup from the heat.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork, pour the syrup over it, and fold gently.
Cover and steam off the heat for 10 minutes so the rice absorbs the sweetness. Serve warm.
Rinse the wheat in several changes of water and soak it in cold water for 2 hours. Drain.
Put the chicken in a large heavy pot with [[8 cups]] water, the cinnamon stick and the salt. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Simmer the chicken for 30 minutes until cooked through to 165°F (74°C). Lift it out and let it cool.
Shred the chicken meat, discarding skin and bones.
Add the drained wheat to the broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring from time to time, until the wheat is very soft.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot. Remove the cinnamon stick.
Beat the mixture hard with a wooden spoon or potato masher for 10 minutes over low heat until it forms a smooth thick porridge. Add a splash of hot water if too stiff.
Spoon into bowls, make a well in the center, and fill it with melted butter. Dust with cinnamon.
Stir the saffron into the hot water and leave it to bloom.
Melt the ghee in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry the vermicelli, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden.
Add the saffron water, sugar and cardamom. Stir and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are tender.
Stir in the rose water and spread the noodles on a platter.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat, pour in the eggs, and cook for 2 minutes per side until fully set with no runny egg.
Lay the omelet over the vermicelli, or cut it into strips, and serve warm.
Mix [[2 cups]] flour and a pinch of salt. Rub in [[3 tbsp]] oil, then add [[0.5 cup]] warm water to make a smooth dough. Knead for 5 minutes, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully cooked to 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the potato, cumin, chili, coriander and salt and cook for 2 minutes. Add the cilantro and let the filling cool.
Mix [[1 tbsp]] flour with a little water to make a thin sealing paste.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into a thin circle. Cut each circle in half.
Fold each half into a cone, fill with a spoonful of filling, and seal the open edge with a dab of paste.
Heat the frying oil in a pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the samboosa in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
Grease a shallow dish with a little ghee.
Whisk the cornstarch with [[1 cup]] cold water until completely smooth.
In a large heavy pot, heat the sugar with [[2 cups]] water until the sugar dissolves. Add the saffron.
Whisk the cornstarch mixture into the pot and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens, about 10 minutes.
Add the melted ghee a little at a time, stirring constantly, as the mixture cooks.
Keep stirring for 30 to 35 minutes until the halwa is dark, glossy and translucent and leaves the sides of the pot.
Stir in the cardamom, rose water and half of the nuts.
Pour into the dish and smooth the top. Sprinkle with the remaining nuts.
Let it cool and set for 2 hours, then cut into squares.

ing: 1 chopped for the stew, 1 finely chopped for the filling
st: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb cubes for 8 minutes, then add 1 chopped onion and the garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric, baharat and salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the dried limes and [[6 cups]] water, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the lamb is tender.
Meanwhile, make the dough by mixing the flour, a pinch of salt and [[0.75 cup]] water. Knead for 5 minutes, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Cook the ground lamb with the finely chopped onion in a dry skillet for 6 minutes until fully cooked to 160°F (71°C). Season with salt and cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut into small circles. Put a little filling in the center of each, fold into half-moons and pinch the edges closed.
Drop the dumplings into the simmering stew one by one. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes until they float and are tender.
Remove the dried limes if you like, and serve the stew hot in deep bowls.
